I have been farming these 10.1 mu for 20 years. I never went to school, but I know my land by walking on it every day. My family has 7 people, and some work in factories, but we still need the grain to eat and sell.

For wheat this winter: I will plant the same improved wheat seed as last year, about 25 jin per mu, sown with the machine. Before sowing, I hire the rotary tiller to chop the maize stubble into the soil — that costs money, but the wheat needs a soft bed. For fertilizer, I put one big bag of compound fertilizer per mu, 50 kg, the kind with the three numbers on it. Then in spring when the wheat turns green, I spread 80 jin of urea per mu — that is 40 kg. My neighbor Aunt Li did exactly this last year and her wheat had big full heads. I irrigate three times: once before winter so the wheat does not freeze, once when it starts jointing in spring, and once when the grain is filling. I spray pesticide twice — once for weeds right after sowing, and once for bugs before the wheat heads. I expect about 960 jin per mu, around 480 kg. Last year I got about that.

For maize this summer: As soon as the wheat comes off the field in June, I plant hybrid maize seed with the no-tillage machine. No plowing — the machine cuts through the wheat straw and puts the seed in. This saves diesel and time. I put one bag of compound fertilizer per mu, 50 kg, at sowing. When the corn is knee-high, I top-dress with 60 jin of urea per mu — 30 kg. I learned this from my cousin; his corn was tall and thick last year. I irrigate once in July or August if the leaves curl from the heat — the well has water, but pumping costs electricity, so I only do it once unless it is very dry. I spray twice — once for weeds at sowing, and once for corn borers if I see holes in the leaves. I expect about 1,100 jin per mu, 550 kg.

Fertilizer is expensive now. Every bag is real money. But I would rather put a little too much than too little. If the harvest fails, my family is in trouble. Wasting some fertilizer is just money lost; a bad harvest is a disaster. I watch what my neighbors do. If everyone on this side of the village applies about this much, then I do too. With 10.1 mu I have some room to buy inputs, but I still think about the whole year — spending more on fertilizer means less for hiring help at harvest. I will stick to what worked before.
